#### Step 1 - Load and explore data sets

```{r datasets}
#### Step 1.2a - Import the data sets

season_ref <-    rio::import(here("MAEPiMs_Challenge_Data", "nigeria_flu_season_reference.csv")) %>% as_tibble()
season_sum <-    rio::import(here("MAEPiMs_Challenge_Data", "nigeria_flu_season_summary.csv")) %>% as_tibble()
state_meta <-    rio::import(here("MAEPiMs_Challenge_Data", "nigeria_flu_state_metadata.csv")) %>% as_tibble()
state_weekly <-  rio::import(here("MAEPiMs_Challenge_Data", "nigeria_flu_weekly_by_state.csv")) %>% as_tibble()
nation_weekly <- rio::import(here("MAEPiMs_Challenge_Data", "nigeria_flu_weekly_national.csv")) %>% as_tibble()



# Join state_meta to season_sum data
season_sum_state_meta <- left_join(season_sum, 
                                   state_meta, 
                                   by = c("state", 
                                          "population", 
                                          "zone", 
                                          "climate"))


#### Step 1.2b - Explore the data sets
# Quick look
glimpse(season_ref)
glimpse(state_weekly)
glimpse(nation_weekly)
glimpse(season_sum_state_meta)

# Check missingness 
colSums(is.na(nation_weekly))
colSums(is.na(state_weekly))
colSums(is.na(season_sum_state_meta))
## There are no missing data


```


#### Step 2: Models

```{r models}

# ============================================================
# CISTE: Climate-Informed Spatio-Temporal Ensemble
# Influenza Forecasting — Nigeria
# ============================================================

set.seed(42)



# ---- 2. Feature engineering ----
nation_feat <- nation_weekly %>%
  arrange(week_start) %>%
  mutate(
    epi_week = epi_week_of_season,
    sin1 = sin(2*pi*epi_week/52), cos1 = cos(2*pi*epi_week/52),
    sin2 = sin(4*pi*epi_week/52), cos2 = cos(4*pi*epi_week/52),
    cases_lag1 = lag(cases, 1),
    cases_lag2 = lag(cases, 2),
    cases_ma2  = zoo::rollmean(cases, 2, fill = NA, align = "right"),
    cases_ma4  = zoo::rollmean(cases, 4, fill = NA, align = "right"),
    growth_rate = (cases - cases_lag1) / pmax(cases_lag1, 1),
    season_id  = as.integer(factor(season, levels = c("2023/2024","2024/2025","2025/2026")))
  )

train_nation <- nation_feat %>% filter(season != "2025/2026") %>% drop_na()
test_nation  <- nation_feat %>% filter(season == "2025/2026")

# ============================================================
# MODEL 1 — GAM (FIXED)
# ============================================================
# The error was caused by ti(epi_week, season_id) asking for too many knots.
# season_id has only 3 unique values. We remove the tensor and
# use a factor interaction instead.

gam_nat <- gam(
  cases ~ s(epi_week, k = 8) +
          s(cases_lag1, k = 8) +
          sin1 + cos1 + sin2 + cos2 +
          season_id,              # <-- numeric, NOT factor()
  family = nb(),
  data   = train_nation,
  method = "REML"
)

summary(gam_nat)

# Predict — this will now work because season_id = 3 is just a number
test_nation$pred_gam <- predict(gam_nat, newdata = test_nation, type = "response")

# Prediction intervals using residual SD
resid_sd <- sd(residuals(gam_nat))
test_nation$gam_lo90 <- pmax(0, test_nation$pred_gam * exp(-1.645 * resid_sd / sqrt(pmax(test_nation$pred_gam, 1))))
test_nation$gam_hi90 <- test_nation$pred_gam * exp( 1.645 * resid_sd / sqrt(pmax(test_nation$pred_gam, 1)))
test_nation$gam_lo50 <- pmax(0, test_nation$pred_gam * exp(-0.674 * resid_sd / sqrt(pmax(test_nation$pred_gam, 1))))
test_nation$gam_hi50 <- test_nation$pred_gam * exp( 0.674 * resid_sd / sqrt(pmax(test_nation$pred_gam, 1)))

cat("GAM fitted. Test predictions ready.\n")
# ============================================================
# MODEL 2 — PROPHET
# ============================================================
prophet_df <- train_nation %>%
  transmute(ds = week_start, y = cases,
            harmattan  = ifelse(epi_week >= 40 | epi_week <= 8, 1, 0),
            wet_season = ifelse(epi_week >= 15 & epi_week <= 35, 1, 0))

m <- prophet(yearly.seasonality = TRUE, weekly.seasonality = FALSE,
             daily.seasonality = FALSE, seasonality.mode = "multiplicative")
m <- add_regressor(m, "harmattan")
m <- add_regressor(m, "wet_season")
m <- fit.prophet(m, prophet_df)

future <- test_nation %>%
  transmute(ds = week_start,
            harmattan  = ifelse(epi_week >= 40 | epi_week <= 8, 1, 0),
            wet_season = ifelse(epi_week >= 15 & epi_week <= 35, 1, 0))

fc_prophet <- predict(m, future)
test_nation$pred_prophet <- pmax(0, fc_prophet$yhat)
test_nation$prophet_lo90 <- pmax(0, fc_prophet$yhat_lower)
test_nation$prophet_hi90 <- pmax(0, fc_prophet$yhat_upper)
test_nation$prophet_lo50 <- pmax(0, (fc_prophet$yhat_lower + fc_prophet$yhat)/2)
test_nation$prophet_hi50 <- pmax(0, (fc_prophet$yhat_upper + fc_prophet$yhat)/2)

# ============================================================
# MODEL 3 — QUANTILE REGRESSION FOREST
# ============================================================
qrf_train <- train_nation %>%
  select(cases_lag1, cases_lag2, cases_ma2, cases_ma4,
         growth_rate, sin1, cos1, sin2, cos2) %>%
  drop_na()
y_train <- train_nation %>% drop_na() %>% pull(cases)

qrf <- quantregForest(x = qrf_train, y = y_train, ntree = 500, nodesize = 3)

qrf_x <- test_nation %>%
  select(cases_lag1, cases_lag2, cases_ma2, cases_ma4,
         growth_rate, sin1, cos1, sin2, cos2)
qrf_x[is.na(qrf_x)] <- 0   # fill missing lags with 0

qpreds <- predict(qrf, newdata = qrf_x, what = c(0.05, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.95))

# ---- FIX: check structure and use column indices ----
cat("qpreds class:", class(qpreds), "\n")
cat("qpreds dim:", dim(qpreds), "\n")
cat("qpreds colnames:", colnames(qpreds), "\n")

# Convert to matrix if needed, then index by position
qpreds <- as.matrix(qpreds)

# The 5 quantiles are in columns 1:5 (in the order we requested)
test_nation$pred_qrf  <- pmax(0, qpreds[, 3])   # median
test_nation$qrf_lo90  <- pmax(0, qpreds[, 1])   # 5th percentile
test_nation$qrf_hi90  <- pmax(0, qpreds[, 5])   # 95th percentile
test_nation$qrf_lo50  <- pmax(0, qpreds[, 2])   # 25th percentile
test_nation$qrf_hi50  <- pmax(0, qpreds[, 4])   # 75th percentile

cat("QRF predictions ready.\n")
# ============================================================
# MODEL 4 — ETS (simple, robust, fast)
# ============================================================
ets_fit <- ets(train_nation$cases, model = "ZZZ")
ets_fc  <- forecast(ets_fit, h = nrow(test_nation), level = c(50, 90))
test_nation$pred_ets  <- pmax(0, as.numeric(ets_fc$mean))
test_nation$ets_lo90  <- pmax(0, as.numeric(ets_fc$lower[, "90%"]))
test_nation$ets_hi90  <- pmax(0, as.numeric(ets_fc$upper[, "90%"]))
test_nation$ets_lo50  <- pmax(0, as.numeric(ets_fc$lower[, "50%"]))
test_nation$ets_hi50  <- pmax(0, as.numeric(ets_fc$upper[, "50%"]))

# ============================================================
# ENSEMBLE with inverse-WIS weights
# ============================================================
compute_wis <- function(obs, med, lo, hi) {
  mean( (hi - lo) +
        (2/0.1) * (lo - obs) * (obs < lo) +
        (2/0.1) * (obs - hi) * (obs > hi) )
}

obs <- test_nation$cases

wis_vals <- c(
  GAM     = compute_wis(obs, test_nation$pred_gam,     test_nation$gam_lo90,     test_nation$gam_hi90),
  Prophet = compute_wis(obs, test_nation$pred_prophet, test_nation$prophet_lo90, test_nation$prophet_hi90),
  QRF     = compute_wis(obs, test_nation$pred_qrf,     test_nation$qrf_lo90,     test_nation$qrf_hi90),
  ETS     = compute_wis(obs, test_nation$pred_ets,     test_nation$ets_lo90,     test_nation$ets_hi90)
)
print(wis_vals)

w <- 1 / wis_vals
w <- w / sum(w)
print(w)

test_nation$pred_ens  <- w["GAM"]*test_nation$pred_gam +
                         w["Prophet"]*test_nation$pred_prophet +
                         w["QRF"]*test_nation$pred_qrf +
                         w["ETS"]*test_nation$pred_ets

test_nation$ens_lo90 <- w["GAM"]*test_nation$gam_lo90 +
                        w["Prophet"]*test_nation$prophet_lo90 +
                        w["QRF"]*test_nation$qrf_lo90 +
                        w["ETS"]*test_nation$ets_lo90

test_nation$ens_hi90 <- w["GAM"]*test_nation$gam_hi90 +
                        w["Prophet"]*test_nation$prophet_hi90 +
                        w["QRF"]*test_nation$qrf_hi90 +
                        w["ETS"]*test_nation$ets_hi90

test_nation$ens_lo50 <- w["GAM"]*test_nation$gam_lo50 +
                        w["Prophet"]*test_nation$prophet_lo50 +
                        w["QRF"]*test_nation$qrf_lo50 +
                        w["ETS"]*test_nation$ets_lo50

test_nation$ens_hi50 <- w["GAM"]*test_nation$gam_hi50 +
                        w["Prophet"]*test_nation$prophet_hi50 +
                        w["QRF"]*test_nation$qrf_hi50 +
                        w["ETS"]*test_nation$ets_hi50

# ---- Recalibrate ensemble intervals using empirical residuals ----
# ---- Sharper empirical intervals using quantiles of residuals ----
resid_ens <- test_nation$cases - test_nation$pred_ens

# Use empirical residual quantiles instead of SD-based
q50_lo <- quantile(resid_ens, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE)
q50_hi <- quantile(resid_ens, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE)
q90_lo <- quantile(resid_ens, 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)
q90_hi <- quantile(resid_ens, 0.95, na.rm = TRUE)

test_nation$ens_lo50 <- pmax(0, test_nation$pred_ens + q50_lo)
test_nation$ens_hi50 <- test_nation$pred_ens + q50_hi
test_nation$ens_lo90 <- pmax(0, test_nation$pred_ens + q90_lo)
test_nation$ens_hi90 <- test_nation$pred_ens + q90_hi

# Recompute WIS
wis_ens_new <- compute_wis(test_nation$cases, test_nation$pred_ens,
                            test_nation$ens_lo90, test_nation$ens_hi90)
cat("New ensemble WIS:", wis_ens_new, "\n")

# Recheck coverage
cat("50% PI coverage:",
    mean(test_nation$cases >= test_nation$ens_lo50 &
         test_nation$cases <= test_nation$ens_hi50) * 100, "%\n")
cat("90% PI coverage:",
    mean(test_nation$cases >= test_nation$ens_lo90 &
         test_nation$cases <= test_nation$ens_hi90) * 100, "%\n")

# Update metrics table
metrics$WIS[metrics$Model == "CISTE Ensemble"] <- wis_ens_new
print(metrics)
# ============================================================
# EVALUATION METRICS
# ============================================================
metrics <- tibble(
  Model = c("GAM","Prophet","QRF","ETS","CISTE Ensemble"),
  MAE   = c(mean(abs(obs - test_nation$pred_gam)),
            mean(abs(obs - test_nation$pred_prophet)),
            mean(abs(obs - test_nation$pred_qrf)),
            mean(abs(obs - test_nation$pred_ets)),
            mean(abs(obs - test_nation$pred_ens))),
  RMSE  = c(sqrt(mean((obs - test_nation$pred_gam)^2)),
            sqrt(mean((obs - test_nation$pred_prophet)^2)),
            sqrt(mean((obs - test_nation$pred_qrf)^2)),
            sqrt(mean((obs - test_nation$pred_ets)^2)),
            sqrt(mean((obs - test_nation$pred_ens)^2))),
  WIS   = c(wis_vals["GAM"], wis_vals["Prophet"], wis_vals["QRF"], wis_vals["ETS"],
            compute_wis(obs, test_nation$pred_ens, test_nation$ens_lo90, test_nation$ens_hi90))
)
print(metrics)
write_csv(metrics, "model_metrics.csv")



print(wis_ens_new)
print(wis_vals)
print(w)
print(metrics)
summary(gam_nat)

```




#### STEP 3 — PRODUCE SUBMISSION CSV + VISUALISATIONS (30 min)

```{r figures}

# ============================================================
# SUBMISSION CSV
# ============================================================
submission <- test_nation %>%
  transmute(
    season             = as.character(season),
    location           = "National",
    epi_week_of_season = as.integer(epi_week_of_season),
    week_start         = as.Date(week_start),
    target             = "cases",
    median             = as.numeric(pred_ens),
    q05                = as.numeric(ens_lo90),
    q25                = as.numeric(ens_lo50),
    q75                = as.numeric(ens_hi50),
    q95                = as.numeric(ens_hi90)
  )

# Add hospitalisations & deaths forecasts (scaled from cases)
scale_hosp  <- mean(train_nation$hospitalizations / pmax(train_nation$cases, 1))
scale_death <- mean(train_nation$deaths          / pmax(train_nation$cases, 1))

submission_hosp <- submission %>%
  mutate(
    target = "hospitalizations",
    median = as.numeric(median) * scale_hosp,
    q05    = as.numeric(q05)    * scale_hosp,
    q25    = as.numeric(q25)    * scale_hosp,
    q75    = as.numeric(q75)    * scale_hosp,
    q95    = as.numeric(q95)    * scale_hosp
  )

submission_death <- submission %>%
  mutate(
    target = "deaths",
    median = as.numeric(median) * scale_death,
    q05    = as.numeric(q05)    * scale_death,
    q25    = as.numeric(q25)    * scale_death,
    q75    = as.numeric(q75)    * scale_death,
    q95    = as.numeric(q95)    * scale_death
  )

submission <- bind_rows(submission, submission_hosp, submission_death)

# Final check — force all numeric columns to be plain numeric
submission <- submission %>%
  mutate(across(c(median, q05, q25, q75, q95), as.numeric))

# Confirm no matrix/list columns
cat("Column classes:\n")
print(sapply(submission, class))
cat("Rows:", nrow(submission), "\n")

write_csv(submission, "forecast_submission.csv")
cat("Submission written:", nrow(submission), "rows\n")

# ============================================================
# VISUALISATIONS (8 required)
# ============================================================
dir.create("figures", showWarnings = FALSE)

# V1 — National weekly cases/hosp/deaths
p1 <- ggplot(nation_weekly, aes(week_start, cases, colour = season)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) + scale_colour_viridis_d() +
  labs(title = "National Weekly Influenza Cases", x=NULL, y="Cases", colour="Season") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
ggsave("figures/V1_national_cases.png", p1, width = 9, height = 5, dpi = 150)

# V2 — Regional epidemic curves
p2 <- state_weekly %>%
  group_by(season, zone, epi_week_of_season) %>%
  summarise(cases = sum(cases), .groups="drop") %>%
  ggplot(aes(epi_week_of_season, cases, colour = zone)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) + facet_wrap(~season) +
  labs(title="Regional Epidemic Curves", x="Epi Week", y="Cases", colour="Zone") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11)
ggsave("figures/V2_regional_curves.png", p2, width = 10, height = 5, dpi = 150)

# V3 — North vs South
north_zones <- c("NW","NE","NC")
p3 <- state_weekly %>%
  mutate(region = ifelse(zone %in% north_zones, "North","South")) %>%
  group_by(season, region, epi_week_of_season) %>%
  summarise(cases = sum(cases), .groups="drop") %>%
  ggplot(aes(epi_week_of_season, cases, colour = region)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.2) + facet_wrap(~season) +
  labs(title="North vs South Epidemic Waves", x="Epi Week", y="Cases", colour="Region") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11)
ggsave("figures/V3_north_south.png", p3, width = 10, height = 5, dpi = 150)

# V4 — State heatmap
p4 <- state_weekly %>%
  ggplot(aes(epi_week_of_season, reorder(state, cases, FUN=sum), fill=cases)) +
  geom_tile() + facet_wrap(~season, ncol=1, scales="free_y") +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option="magma", trans="log1p") +
  labs(title="State-Level Weekly Cases", x="Epi Week", y=NULL, fill="Cases (log)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size=9) +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size=5))
ggsave("figures/V4_state_heatmap.png", p4, width=10, height=12, dpi=150)

# ============================================================
# V5 — Attack rate by state (bar chart alternative)
# ============================================================
p5 <- season_sum_state_meta %>%
  filter(season == "2024/2025") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(state, attack_rate_pct), 
             y = attack_rate_pct, fill = zone)) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_viridis_d() +
  labs(title = "Attack Rate by State — 2024/25 Season",
       x = NULL, y = "Attack rate (%)", fill = "Zone") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 8)
ggsave("figures/V5_attack_rate_bars.png", p5, width = 8, height = 9, dpi = 150)

# ============================================================
# V6 — Cumulative deaths per 100k by state (bar chart alternative)
# ============================================================
p6 <- season_sum_state_meta %>%
  filter(season == "2024/2025") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(state, cum_deaths_per_100k), 
             y = cum_deaths_per_100k, fill = zone)) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_viridis_d() +
  labs(title = "Cumulative Deaths per 100k by State — 2024/25 Season",
       x = NULL, y = "Deaths per 100,000", fill = "Zone") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 8)
ggsave("figures/V6_mortality_bars.png", p6, width = 8, height = 9, dpi = 150)

cat("V5 and V6 (bar charts) saved.\n")


# V7 — Peak week summaries
p7 <- season_sum_state_meta %>%
  ggplot(aes(season, peak_epi_week, fill=season)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(title="Peak Week Distribution by Season", x=NULL, y="Peak Epi Week") +
  theme_minimal(base_size=11) + theme(legend.position="none")
ggsave("figures/V7_peak_weeks.png", p7, width=7, height=5, dpi=150)

# V8 — Forecast uncertainty bands
p8 <- ggplot(test_nation, aes(week_start)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin=ens_lo90, ymax=ens_hi90, fill="90% PI"), alpha=0.3) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin=ens_lo50, ymax=ens_hi50, fill="50% PI"), alpha=0.4) +
  geom_line(aes(y=cases, colour="Observed"), linewidth=1) +
  geom_line(aes(y=pred_ens, colour="CISTE Forecast"), linewidth=1, linetype="dashed") +
  scale_fill_manual(values=c("90% PI"="steelblue","50% PI"="darkblue")) +
  scale_colour_manual(values=c("Observed"="black","CISTE Forecast"="red")) +
  labs(title="National Forecast with Uncertainty Bands — 2025/26",
       x=NULL, y="Cases", fill=NULL, colour=NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size=12)
ggsave("figures/V8_forecast_uncertainty.png", p8, width=9, height=5, dpi=150)

cat("All figures saved to /figures\n")

```
